Loses in thought, he missed his bus stop.

cz.st: ___ in thought, he missed his bus stop.

items.rule: ‘생각에 빠진’ 수동 상태이므로 과거분사(Lost)를 써요.

items.good: Not wanting to be late, Sam ran to the station.
items.ko: 늦고 싶지 않아서 샘은 역까지 달려갔다.
bad: Not wanted to be late, Sam ran to the station.
Not want to be late, Sam ran to the station.
Not wants to be late, Sam ran to the station.

cz.st: Not ___ to be late, Sam ran to the station.

items.rule: 이유를 나타내는 부정 분사구문: Not + -ing.

items.good: Closing her eyes, she made a wish.
items.ko: 눈을 감고 그녀는 소원을 빌었다.
bad: Closed her eyes, she made a wish.
Close her eyes, she made a wish.
Closes her eyes, she made a wish.

cz.st: ___ her eyes, she made a wish.

items.rule: 목적어(her eyes)를 갖는 능동 동작은 -ing 분사구문으로 나타내요.

items.good: Covered with snow, the mountain looked like a giant cake.
items.ko: 눈으로 덮여 그 산은 거대한 케이크처럼 보였다.
bad: Covering with snow, the mountain looked like a giant cake.
Cover with snow, the mountain looked like a giant cake.
Covers with snow, the mountain looked like a giant cake.

cz.st: ___ with snow, the mountain looked like a giant cake.

items.rule: 산은 ‘덮인’ 수동 관계이므로 과거분사(Covered)를 써요. be covered with ~.

items.good: Built in 1920, the old station is now a museum.
items.ko: 1920년에 지어진 그 옛 역은 지금은 박물관이다.
bad: Building in 1920, the old station is now a museum.
Build in 1920, the old station is now a museum.
Builds in 1920, the old station is now a museum.

cz.st: ___ in 1920, the old station is now a museum.

items.rule: 역은 ‘지어진’ 수동 관계이므로 과거분사(Built)를 써요.

items.good: Hoping to win a prize, Mia practiced every day.
items.ko: 상을 타기를 바라며 미아는 매일 연습했다.
bad: Hoped to win a prize, Mia practiced every day.
Hope to win a prize, Mia practiced every day.
Hopes to win a prize, Mia practiced every day.

cz.st: ___ to win a prize, Mia practiced every day.

items.rule: 주어가 ‘바라는’ 능동 관계이고 이유·목적의 뜻이므로 -ing 분사구문이에요.

items.q: “Because she felt lonely, Hana called her friend.”를 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?
o: Feeling lonely, Hana called her friend.
Felt lonely, Hana called her friend.
Because feeling lonely, Hana called her friend.
Feeling lonely, her friend was called by Hana.
items.why: 접속사 Because와 주어를 지우고 felt를 Feeling으로 바꾼 'Feeling lonely, Hana called her friend.'가 맞아요. 'Feeling lonely, her friend was called by Hana.'는 의미상 주어가 her friend가 되어 틀려요.

items.q: “As the singer was surrounded by fans, she smiled.”을 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?
o: Surrounded by fans, the singer smiled.
Surrounding by fans, the singer smiled.
Being surrounding by fans, the singer smiled.
Surround by fans, the singer smiled.
items.why: 가수는 팬들에게 ‘둘러싸인’ 수동 관계이므로 과거분사 Surrounded를 써요.

items.q: “When Minho opened the box, he found a letter.”를 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?
o: Opening the box, Minho found a letter.
Opening the box, a letter was found by Minho.
Opened the box, Minho found a letter.
Minho opening the box, he found a letter.
items.why: 주절의 주어(Minho)와 분사의 의미상 주어가 같아야 해요. 주어가 같으면 종속절의 주어를 반복하지 않아요.

items.q: “After I had read the book, I returned it to the library.”를 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?
o: Having read the book, I returned it to the library.
Having reading the book, I returned it to the library.
Having been read the book, I returned it to the library.
Had read the book, I returned it to the library.
items.why: 분사구문의 동작이 주절보다 먼저 끝났으므로 완료형 Having + 과거분사를 써요.

items.q: “Because he didn't have any money, Ken couldn't buy lunch.”를 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?
o: Not having any money, Ken couldn't buy lunch.
Not had any money, Ken couldn't buy lunch.
Don't having any money, Ken couldn't buy lunch.
Having no any money, Ken couldn't buy lunch.
items.why: 부정 분사구문은 Not + -ing로 써요. 분사구문 안에 do동사는 쓰지 않아요.

items.q: “Since the road had been closed by snow, the bus took another route.”를 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?
o: The road having been closed by snow, the bus took another route.
Having been closed by snow, the bus took another route.
The road been closed by snow, the bus took another route.
The road having closed by snow, the bus took another route.
items.why: 종속절 주어(the road)가 주절 주어(the bus)와 다르므로 주어를 남기고, 완료 수동은 having been + 과거분사로 써요.

items.q: “If you turn right at the bank, you'll find the post office.”를 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?
o: Turning right at the bank, you'll find the post office.
Turned right at the bank, you'll find the post office.
Turns right at the bank, you'll find the post office.
To turn right at the bank, you'll find the post office.
items.why: 주어(you)가 직접 방향을 ‘도는’ 능동 관계이므로 현재분사 Turning을 써요.

items.q: “While she was waiting for the bus, Eve read a book.”을 접속사를 남기고 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?
o: While waiting for the bus, Eve read a book.
While waited for the bus, Eve read a book.
While wait for the bus, Eve read a book.
While to wait for the bus, Eve read a book.
items.why: ‘주어 + be동사’를 생략하고 접속사 While 뒤에 -ing를 남겨요.

items.q: “Walking along the beach, Sora found a shell.”과 같은 뜻의 문장은?
o: While Sora was walking along the beach, she found a shell.
While Sora walks along the beach, she found a shell.
Because Sora found a shell, she walked along the beach.
When Sora was walked along the beach, she found a shell.
items.why: 분사구문의 시제는 주절을 따라 과거예요. 해변을 걷는 동안 조개를 발견했다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: “Not wanting to disturb her, I left quietly.”와 같은 뜻의 문장은?
o: Because I did not want to disturb her, I left quietly.
When I wanted to disturb her, I left quietly.
If I do not want to disturb her, I left quietly.
Because I disturbed her, I did not want to leave quietly.
items.why: Not + -ing 분사구문은 여기서 ‘~하고 싶지 않아서’라는 이유를 나타내요.

items.q: “Seen from the sky, the island looks like a heart.”와 같은 뜻의 문장은?
o: When it is seen from the sky, the island looks like a heart.
When it sees the sky, the island looks like a heart.
Although it is seen from the sky, the island looks like a heart.
Because the island looked at the sky, it looks like a heart.
items.why: Seen은 수동 의미이므로 절로 바꾸면 it is seen이 돼요.

items.q: “Having missed the last train, they took a taxi.”와 같은 뜻의 문장은?
o: Because they had missed the last train, they took a taxi.
Because they missed the last train, they will take a taxi.
After they took a taxi, they had missed the last train.
As they miss the last train, they took a taxi.
items.why: 완료 분사구문은 주절보다 앞선 일을 나타내므로 절에서는 had missed가 돼요.

items.q: “Weather permitting, the match will be held on Sunday.”와 같은 뜻의 문장은?
o: If the weather permits, the match will be held on Sunday.
Unless the weather permits, the match will be held on Sunday.
If the weather permitted, the match will be held on Sunday.
Although the weather permits, the match will not be held on Sunday.
items.why: Weather permitting은 ‘날씨가 허락하면’이라는 조건이에요. unless는 반대 뜻이 돼요.

items.q: “The meeting being over, everyone went home.”와 같은 뜻의 문장은?
o: After the meeting was over, everyone went home.
Before the meeting was over, everyone went home.
Although the meeting was over, everyone stayed there.
While the meeting is over, everyone went home.
items.why: 독립분사구문 The meeting being over는 ‘회의가 끝난 뒤(끝났으므로)’의 뜻이에요.

items.q: “Having no one to talk to, Daeho felt lonely.”와 같은 뜻의 문장은?
o: Since he had no one to talk to, Daeho felt lonely.
If he has no one to talk to, Daeho felt lonely.
After he talked to everyone, Daeho felt lonely.
Although he had no one to talk to, Daeho felt lonely.
items.why: Having no one ~은 이유를 나타내므로 Since/Because를 써서 바꿔요.

items.q: “Being a doctor, she knows how to treat a fever.”에서 분사구문이 나타내는 의미는?
o: 이유·원인
양보·대조
조건·가정
시간·순서
items.why: ‘의사이기 때문에’ 열을 치료할 줄 안다는 뜻이므로 이유예요.

items.q: “The train left at six, arriving in Daegu at nine.”에서 분사구문이 나타내는 의미는?
o: 결과·연속 동작
이유·원인
양보·대조
조건·가정
items.why: 문장 뒤에 오는 -ing는 ‘그리고 ~했다’처럼 이어지는 결과나 연속 동작을 나타내요.

items.q: “Reaching the top of the hill, we sat down to rest.”에서 분사구문이 나타내는 의미는?
o: 시간·때
이유·원인
양보·대조
조건·가정
items.why: ‘언덕 꼭대기에 닿았을 때’라는 뜻의 시간이에요.

items.q: “Left in direct sunlight, chocolate melts quickly.”에서 분사구문이 나타내는 의미는?
o: 조건·가정
이유·원인
양보·대조
결과·연속 동작
items.why: ‘햇빛에 그대로 두면’이라는 뜻이므로 조건이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 분사구문이 양보(~이지만)의 뜻을 나타내는 문장은?
o: Living near the sea, Dan can't swim.
Feeling dizzy, Rina sat down at once.
Opening the box, Tom began to smile.
Turning off the light, you can save energy.
items.why: 바다 근처에 살지만 수영을 못한다는 뜻이라 양보예요. 나머지는 각각 이유, 시간, 조건에 가까워요.

items.q: “Driving to work, ___.” 빈칸에 알맞은 절은?
o: Dad heard a strange noise from the engine
a strange noise came from the engine
the engine made a strange noise for him
it was noisy from the engine
items.why: Driving의 의미상 주어는 사람이어야 해요. 엔진이나 소리는 운전할 수 없으므로 나머지는 틀려요.

items.q: “Climbing the mountain, ___.” 빈칸에 알맞은 절은?
o: the hikers enjoyed a lovely view
a lovely view appeared before our eyes
the trail seemed shorter to us
the weather made it very hard
items.why: ‘올라가는’ 주체가 주절의 주어여야 해요. 보기 중 hikers만 산을 오를 수 있어요.

items.q: “Having eaten too much, ___.” 빈칸에 알맞은 절은?
o: I felt sick for the whole evening
the greasy pizza made me feel quite sick
a bad stomachache began very quickly
my stomach started to hurt badly
items.why: 먹은 사람이 주절의 주어여야 해요. 피자, 복통, 배는 ‘먹은’ 주체가 될 수 없어요.

items.q: 분사구문의 의미상 주어가 어색한 문장은?
o: Reading in bed, the lamp suddenly went out.
Waiting for the bus, I checked my phone.
Surprised by the noise, the baby started to cry.
Having lost his keys, Joon had to call his mother.
items.why: Reading의 주체는 사람인데 주절의 주어는 the lamp라서 어색해요(현수 분사구문).

items.q: 분사구문의 주어가 주절의 주어와 맞지 않아 어색한 문장은?
o: Stuck in the elevator, the lights went out.
Surprised by the result, the team cheered loudly.
Lost in the forest, the children stayed calm.
Having cleaned the room, Ella took a short rest.
items.why: ‘갇힌’ 것은 the lights가 아니라 사람이어야 해요.

items.q: “Running for the bus, my bag fell off my shoulder.”를 바르게 고친 문장은?
o: As I ran for the bus, my bag fell off my shoulder.
Running for the bus, my bag was falling off my shoulder.
Having run for the bus, my bag fell off my shoulder.
Ran for the bus, my bag fell off my shoulder.
items.why: 가방은 달릴 수 없으므로 분사구문의 주어가 어긋나요. 절로 풀어 쓰면 해결돼요.

items.q: 분사구문의 주어가 주절의 주어와 달라도 맞는 문장은?
o: The sun having set, the park became quiet.
Having set, the park became quiet.
The sun have set, the park became quiet.
The sun set, the park became quiet.
items.why: 주어가 다르면 분사 앞에 주어를 남겨요(독립분사구문). 나머지는 주어가 어긋나거나 동사 형태가 틀려요.

items.q: 분사구문으로 바꿀 때 종속절의 주어를 지울 수 없는 문장은?
o: As Hana was kind, everyone liked her.
Because he was sleepy, he went to bed.
When she saw the snake, she screamed.
After I finished lunch, I took a walk.
items.why: 종속절과 주절의 주어가 다르면(Hana / everyone) 주어를 남겨서 독립분사구문으로 써야 해요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
___ in a hurry, the report had many mistakes.
o: Written
Writing
Having written
Writes
items.why: 보고서는 ‘쓰인’ 수동 관계이므로 Written이에요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
The boys ran across the field, ___ at the top of their voices.
o: shouting
shouted
shout
to be shouted
items.why: 뒤에 붙는 동시 동작은 -ing로 나타내요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
The man ___ at the gate is our new neighbor.
o: waiting
waited
waits
wait
items.why: 명사를 뒤에서 꾸미며 ‘기다리고 있는’ 능동 관계이므로 -ing예요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
The letter ___ yesterday has not arrived yet.
o: sent
sending
sends
to send
items.why: 편지는 ‘보내진’ 수동 관계이므로 과거분사 sent예요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
The children, ___ by the magician's tricks, clapped their hands.
o: amazed
amazing
amaze
amazes
items.why: 아이들이 놀람을 ‘느끼는’ 쪽이므로 과거분사 amazed예요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
With the lights ___, the theater was completely dark.
o: turned off
turning off
turn off
turns off
items.why: with + 목적어 + 분사: 불이 ‘꺼진’ 수동 관계이므로 과거분사를 써요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
She kept walking with her dog ___ behind her.
o: following
followed
follow
follows
items.why: 개가 ‘따라오는’ 능동 관계이므로 현재분사 following이에요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
___ no reply, Kim sent a second message.
o: Getting
Gotten
Get
Gets
items.why: Kim이 ‘받지 못한’ 능동 관계의 분사구문이므로 Getting이에요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
The first prize, ___ by a ten-year-old girl, surprised everyone.
o: won
winning
win
wins
items.why: 상은 ‘받아진’ 수동 관계이므로 과거분사 won이에요.

items.q:
빈칸 (A), (B)에 알맞은 짝은?
(A) ___ to music, Ben did his homework.
(B) ___ by the loud music, Ben couldn't sleep.
o: (A) Listening (B) Disturbed
(A) Listened (B) Disturbing
(A) Listening (B) Disturbing
(A) Listened (B) Disturbed
items.why: Ben이 음악을 ‘듣는’ 것은 능동(Listening), 음악 때문에 ‘방해받는’ 것은 수동(Disturbed)이에요.

items.q: “그는 눈을 감은 채 노래를 불렀다.”를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
o: He sang with his eyes closed.
He sang with his eyes closing.
He sang with closed his eyes.
He sang with his eyes to close.
items.why: with + 목적어 + 과거분사: 눈은 ‘감겨진’ 상태예요.

items.q: “그녀는 다리를 꼰 채 앉아 있었다.”를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
o: She was sitting with her legs crossed.
She was sitting with her legs crossing.
She was sitting with crossed her legs.
She was sitting with her legs crosses.
items.why: 다리는 ‘꼬인’ 상태이므로 수동 관계의 과거분사 crossed를 써요.

items.q: “그 소년은 편지를 읽는 동안 울었다.”(동시 동작)를 나타내는 문장은?
o: Reading the letter, the boy cried.
Having read the letter, the boy cried.
Having been read the letter, the boy cried.
Read the letter, the boy cried.
items.why: 동시에 일어난 일은 -ing로 나타내요. Having read는 ‘읽은 뒤에’라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: “Because Tom had not studied, he failed the test.”를 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?
o: Not having studied, Tom failed the test.
Not studied, Tom failed the test.
Not having study, Tom failed the test.
Not to have studied, Tom failed the test.
items.why: 먼저 일어난 일의 부정은 Not having + 과거분사로 써요.

items.q: “Having bought the tickets, Jenny went to the cinema.”에서 일어난 순서는?
o: 표를 산 뒤에 영화관에 갔다
영화관에 간 뒤에 표를 샀다
표를 사면서 영화관에 갔다
표를 사지 않고 영화관에 갔다
items.why: 완료 분사구문(Having + 과거분사)은 주절보다 먼저 일어난 일을 나타내요.

items.q: “Generally speaking, summers in Korea are hot and humid.”에서 Generally speaking과 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 표현은?
o: In general
In particular
For a while
At first
items.why: Generally speaking은 ‘일반적으로’라는 뜻으로 In general과 같아요.

items.q: “Judging from his accent, he must be from the south.”에서 Judging from의 뜻은?
o: ~로 판단하면
~에도 불구하고
~을 제외하면
~보다 먼저
items.why: Judging from ~은 ‘~로 판단하면’이라는 뜻의 관용 표현이에요.

items.q: “Considering her age, she plays the violin very well.”에서 Considering의 뜻은?
o: ~을 고려하면
~을 무시하면
~ 때문에
~ 이후에
items.why: Considering ~은 ‘~을 고려하면, ~치고는’이라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 분사구문의 부정형이 틀린 문장은?
o: Don't knowing the way, we asked a stranger.
Not wanting to wake the baby, she whispered.
Never having seen snow, the boy ran outside.
Not having been told, Jay arrived late.
items.why: 분사구문에서는 do동사를 쓰지 않고 Not + -ing로 써요.

items.q: 완료 분사구문이 틀린 문장은?
o: Having ate lunch, Sam went back to work.
Having overslept, Tim missed the first bus.
Having been praised by the coach, Lee smiled.
Having cooked dinner, Mom called us to the table.
items.why: Having 뒤에는 과거분사가 와야 해요. ate가 아니라 eaten이에요.

items.q: with + 목적어 + 분사 구문이 틀린 문장은?
o: My brother stood at the door with his shoes taking off.
Tom sat with his arms folded.
The cat sat by the door with its ears pointing up.
Mia walked with her hair blowing in the wind.
items.why: 신발은 ‘벗겨진’ 수동 관계이므로 with his shoes off 또는 taken off가 맞아요.

items.q: 수동 의미의 분사구문이 올바르게 쓰인 문장은?
o: Written by a famous poet, this poem is loved by many.
Written by a famous poet, I enjoyed this poem very much.
Writing by a famous poet, this poem is loved by many.
Writes by a famous poet, this poem is loved by many.
items.why: ‘쓰인’ 것은 시이므로 주절의 주어도 this poem이어야 해요. 'Written by a famous poet, I enjoyed this poem very much.'는 주어가 I라서 틀려요.

items.q: “창밖을 바라보며 그는 한숨을 쉬었다.”를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
o: Looking out the window, he sighed.
Looked out the window, he sighed.
He sighed, looked out the window.
Looking out the window, a sigh was heard.
items.why: 동시 동작은 -ing 분사구문으로 나타내요. 주어(he)와 분사의 의미상 주어가 일치해야 해요.

items.q: “그녀는 음악을 들으며 숙제를 했다.”를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
o: She did her homework listening to music.
She did her homework listened to music.
She did her homework listen to music.
She did her homework to listening to music.
items.why: 문장 뒤에 -ing를 붙이면 ‘~하면서’라는 동시 동작을 나타낼 수 있어요.

items.q: “그는 방을 나가면서 뒤로 문을 닫았다.”를 분사구문으로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
o: He left the room, closing the door behind him.
He left the room, closed the door behind him.
He left the room, to closing the door behind him.
He left the room, closes the door behind him.
items.why: 연속 동작은 문장 뒤에 -ing 분사구문으로 이어 붙여요.

items.q: 두 문장의 뜻이 서로 다른 것은?
o: Having eaten dinner, I washed the dishes. = I washed the dishes before I ate dinner.
Not knowing the way, I asked a police officer. = As I did not know the way, I asked a police officer.
Walking home, Joon saw a rainbow. = While Joon was walking home, he saw a rainbow.
Seen from afar, the tower looks small. = When it is seen from afar, the tower looks small.
items.why: Having eaten은 ‘먹은 뒤에’라는 뜻이므로 먹기 전에 설거지했다는 풀이는 틀려요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 접속사는?
___ crossing the street, always look both ways.
o: When
Although
Whereas
Unless
items.why: 접속사를 남긴 분사구문에서 ‘길을 건널 때’라는 뜻을 나타내려면 When을 써요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 접속사는?
___ small, the robot can lift heavy boxes.
o: Though
Because
Unless
Since
items.why: 작지만 무거운 상자를 든다는 양보의 뜻이므로 Though예요.

items.q: “Entering the room, the phone rang.”이 어색한 이유는?
o: 의미상 주어가 the phone으로 읽히기 때문에
동사 ring이 과거형이기 때문에
enter가 목적어를 취할 수 없기 때문에
정관사 the를 쓰면 안 되기 때문에
items.why: Entering의 주체는 주절의 주어와 같아야 하는데 전화기는 방에 들어갈 수 없어요.

items.q: 분사구문에서 접속사를 지우지 않고 남겨 두는 가장 큰 이유는?
o: 절 사이의 의미 관계를 분명히 하기 위해서
문장을 더 길고 화려하게 만들기 위해서
주절의 주어를 다른 사람으로 바꾸기 위해서
동사의 시제를 완전히 없애기 위해서
items.why: 접속사를 남기면 시간·양보 등 관계가 또렷해져요(예: While walking, Though tired).

items.q: 완료 분사구문 Having + 과거분사가 쓰이는 때는?
o: 분사구문의 동작이 주절의 동작보다 먼저 일어났을 때
두 동작이 정확히 동시에 일어났을 때
분사구문의 동작이 주절보다 나중에 일어났을 때
주어가 서로 달라서 생략할 때
items.why: 완료형은 한 시제 앞선 일을 나타내요.

items.title: Life in a Tide Pool
items.text: Standing on the rocky shore at low tide, you can find a tiny world hidden in the pools left by the sea. Protected from the waves, small crabs and sea stars live there quietly. Their lives are not easy, however. Heated by the sun, the shallow water can become much warmer than the open sea, and the animals must cope with the sudden change. When the tide returns, fresh cold water rushes in, bringing food and cooling everything down. Having survived such changes every day, tide pool animals have become very tough. Scientists study them, hoping to learn how living things may react to a warmer planet.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How tide pool animals deal with daily change
Why scientists prefer the sea to rocky shores for their research
Which sea animals are the most dangerous to people at low tide
How the open sea becomes warmer than the land every summer
qs.why: 지문은 밀물과 썰물, 햇빛으로 계속 변하는 환경에서 조수 웅덩이 동물이 어떻게 견디는지를 설명해요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what happens when the tide returns?
o: Cold water brings in food and cools the pools.
The pools dry out and the crabs move to other rocks.
Warm water pushes the sea stars onto the open shore.
The waves hide the pools from the scientists for a month.
qs.why: “fresh cold water rushes in, bringing food and cooling everything down”에 나와 있어요.

qs.q: In “Heated by the sun, the shallow water can become much warmer,” what is heated by the sun?
o: the shallow water
the open sea
the small crabs
the rocky shore
qs.why: 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 주절의 주어인 the shallow water예요.

qs.q: The word “tough” in the passage is closest in meaning to
o: strong
rude
lonely
quiet
qs.why: 매일 변화를 견뎌 냈으니 ‘강인한’ 동물이 되었다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why do scientists study tide pool animals?
o: They hope to learn how life may react to a warmer planet.
They want to move the animals into home aquariums for sale.
They need to find out why the tide goes in and out each day.
They plan to make the shallow pools colder during the summer.
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 hoping to learn how living things may react to a warmer planet이라고 해요.

items.title: The Last Bus
items.text: Mina ran down the hill, her bag bouncing against her back. Seeing the lights of the last bus, she waved both arms and shouted. The driver, noticing her at the last moment, stopped a few meters ahead. Out of breath, Mina climbed aboard and thanked him. “Cutting it close again?” he said, smiling. She laughed, too embarrassed to answer. Sitting by the window, she watched the dark town slide past. Having worked on her science project since morning, she was so tired that her eyes closed before the third stop. When the bus finally reached her street, the driver gently called her name.

qs.q: Why did the driver stop a few meters ahead of Mina?
o: He saw her only at the last moment.
He wanted to check her bus pass first.
A fallen tree was blocking the road ahead.
Another passenger had asked him to stop there.
qs.why: “noticing her at the last moment, stopped a few meters ahead”가 근거예요.

qs.q: How did Mina feel when the driver teased her?
o: Embarrassed
Frightened
Disappointed
Confused
qs.why: “too embarrassed to answer”라고 해요.

qs.q: Why did Mina's eyes close before the third stop?
o: She had worked hard on a project all day.
She had run a long race earlier that afternoon.
The seat was warm and the bus ride was very long.
She had stayed awake the whole night before.
qs.why: 과학 프로젝트를 아침부터 해서 매우 피곤했다는 내용이 있어요.

qs.q: The phrase “slide past” suggests that the town
o: moved by smoothly outside the window
stopped at every corner for her
looked bright and noisy to her
seemed to be changing its shape
qs.why: 창밖 풍경이 부드럽게 지나가는 모습을 표현해요.

qs.q: What does the driver do when the bus reaches Mina's street?
o: He calls her name in a gentle voice.
He turns on the lights in the bus.
He drives past her street by mistake.
He asks her to get off at once.
qs.why: 마지막 문장에 gently called her name이라고 나와요.

items.title: Phones and Sleep
items.text: Many teenagers keep their phones beside the bed, scrolling through videos until late at night. Though entertaining, this habit can damage sleep. The bright screen sends a signal to the brain that it is still daytime, delaying the release of the hormone that makes us sleepy. Researchers also found that students, tempted by new messages, often wake up several times during the night. Having slept badly, they find it harder to concentrate at school the next day. Experts therefore advise turning off screens an hour before bedtime and charging the phone in another room. Following this simple advice, many families report calmer mornings and better moods.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Phone habits that disturb teenagers' sleep
The best phones for students who study late at night
How families can choose a quiet bedroom for homework
Why teenagers should avoid watching videos at school
qs.why: 늦은 밤 휴대폰 사용이 수면을 해치는 이유와 해결책을 다뤄요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what does bright light from a screen do to the brain?
o: It makes the brain think it is still daytime.
It helps the brain remember the day's lessons.
It tells the body to eat more in the evening.
It slows the heart so the body feels cold.
qs.why: “sends a signal to the brain that it is still daytime”이라고 해요.

qs.q: In “tempted by new messages,” who is tempted?
o: students
researchers
experts
families
qs.why: 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 바로 앞의 students예요.

qs.q: The word “delaying” in the passage is closest in meaning to
o: putting off
speeding up
keeping safe
copying exactly
qs.why: 호르몬 분비를 ‘늦추는’ 것이므로 put off와 비슷해요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention “calmer mornings and better moods”?
o: To show that the advice has helped some families
To prove that teenagers dislike getting up early
To explain why experts study the brain at night
To warn readers that phones cause bad moods
qs.why: 조언을 따른 가정에서 좋아진 결과를 보여 주기 위해서예요.

items.title: Hanji Paper
items.text: Hanji is a traditional Korean paper made from the inner bark of the mulberry tree. Making it by hand takes many steps. First, the bark is boiled and beaten until it turns into soft fibers. Mixed with water and a natural plant glue, these fibers are scooped onto a screen and shaken gently, forming a thin, even sheet. Dried in the sun, the sheets become strong yet light. Because of this strength, hanji has been used for doors, windows, books, and even clothing. Compared with ordinary paper, it lasts much longer, and some hanji documents have survived for hundreds of years. Today, artists use hanji for lamps and crafts, giving an old material a new life.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A traditional paper, how it is made, and how it is used
The history of the mulberry tree in Korean villages
How artists chose lamps over books and clothing
Why machines make better paper than people do
qs.why: 한지의 재료, 만드는 과정, 쓰임새를 설명하는 글이에요.

qs.q: Which step comes just after the fibers become soft?
o: They are mixed with water and plant glue.
They are dried in the sun for several days.
They are sewn into clothing right away.
They are painted in bright colors first.
qs.why: 섬유가 부드러워진 다음 물과 닥풀을 섞는 단계가 나와요.

qs.q: Why has hanji been used for doors and windows?
o: It is strong yet light.
It is cheaper than any other paper.
It can be made in a few minutes.
It turns white when the sun shines.
qs.why: “Because of this strength”가 이유예요. 강하면서도 가볍다고 했어요.

qs.q: The word “survived” in the passage is closest in meaning to
o: lasted
changed
disappeared
improved
qs.why: 문서가 수백 년 동안 ‘남아 있다’는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: The last sentence suggests that hanji
o: is still valuable in modern life
is no longer made by hand
has become harder to find
is only used in museums
qs.why: 예술가들이 오늘날에도 램프와 공예에 쓴다는 내용에서 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Bike Share Days
items.text: When the city introduced a bike-sharing program, many residents doubted it would work. Worried about theft and traffic, the council started with only fifty bikes in the downtown area. Within a month, however, every bike was being used several times a day. Commuters, avoiding crowded buses, rode to work, while tourists, carrying maps on their phones, explored the old streets. Encouraged by this success, the council added three hundred bikes and new lanes. Not everyone is happy, though. Some shop owners complain that parked bikes block the sidewalks. The council, listening carefully, has promised to build special parking areas next year.

qs.q: How many bikes did the program start with?
o: Fifty
One hundred and fifty
Three hundred
Five thousand
qs.why: 첫 문장들에서 only fifty bikes라고 해요.

qs.q: Why did the council add more bikes and new lanes?
o: The first bikes had been very popular.
Shop owners had asked for more bicycles.
The tourists had complained about the buses.
The old streets had been closed to cars.
qs.why: “Encouraged by this success”는 초기 성공 때문이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why did commuters ride bikes, according to the passage?
o: They wanted to avoid crowded buses.
They wanted to see the old streets.
They had lost their maps on the way.
They were afraid of the rising traffic.
qs.why: “Commuters, avoiding crowded buses”가 근거예요.

qs.q: “Not everyone is happy, though” introduces
o: a problem some people see
a plan for the next year
a lesson from the tourists
a rule about helmets
qs.why: though 뒤에 상점 주인들의 불만이 이어져요.

qs.q: How does the writer present the council?
o: As willing to respond to people's concerns
As careless about the rules of the city
As afraid of the opinions of shop owners
As slow to notice that bikes were popular
qs.why: 불만을 듣고 주차장을 짓겠다고 약속하므로 주민의 걱정에 응답하는 모습이에요.

items.title: Grandma's Kimchi Stew
items.text: Every winter, my grandmother makes kimchi stew in a big black pot. Entering her kitchen, I am always greeted by the warm smell of garlic and sour kimchi. She never uses a recipe. Stirring the pot slowly, she tastes it, adds a pinch of salt, and tastes it again. Once, wanting to help, I measured everything with a spoon and wrote the numbers down. She laughed, saying that the numbers would change with every pot of kimchi. “The stew will tell you what it needs,” she said. Now, living far from home, I make the stew myself, listening for her voice each time I taste it.

qs.q: What did the grandmother mean by “The stew will tell you what it needs”?
o: Cooks should taste and adjust as they go.
The stew needs more water than most cooks think.
Only old kimchi can make a good stew.
Writing numbers down always spoils the taste.
qs.why: 레시피 대신 맛을 보며 조절하라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What did the writer do when trying to help?
o: Measured the ingredients and wrote down the amounts
Bought a new pot at the market near her house
Taught the grandmother a new recipe from a book
Added extra salt to the stew without telling her
qs.why: 숟가락으로 재료를 재고 숫자를 적었다고 해요.

qs.q: How does the writer feel about the grandmother?
o: Warm and respectful
Bored and impatient
Angry and jealous
Shy and worried
qs.why: 할머니의 말을 떠올리며 따라 요리하므로 따뜻하고 존경하는 마음이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the writer now?
o: The writer lives away from home but keeps the tradition.
The writer has stopped cooking and eating kimchi stew.
The writer has moved into the grandmother's house nearby.
The writer buys the stew from a shop every winter now.
qs.why: far from home이지만 직접 끓이며 할머니 목소리를 떠올려요.

items.title: Marathon Morning
items.text: At six o'clock on a cold October morning, Jiho stood at the starting line, shaking his hands to keep them warm. He had trained for five months, running before school, after school, and sometimes in the rain. Now, surrounded by thousands of runners, he felt both excited and afraid. When the horn sounded, the crowd moved forward like a slow river. Jiho kept a steady pace, remembering his coach's advice: start slowly. By the halfway point, his legs ached, but cheering strangers along the road gave him new energy. Crossing the finish line, he did not care about his time. He had finished, and that was enough.

qs.q: What does the passage show about Jiho's goal?
o: Finishing mattered more to him than a fast time.
He wanted to beat every runner around him.
He hoped to impress his coach with his speed.
He planned to quit at the halfway point.
qs.why: 마지막에 시간은 신경 쓰지 않았고 완주만으로 충분했다고 해요.

qs.q: What advice from his coach did Jiho follow?
o: To start slowly
To run only in dry weather
To stay close to the crowd
To drink water at every corner
qs.why: “remembering his coach's advice: start slowly”가 근거예요.

qs.q: The phrase “steady pace” means
o: an even speed
a very fast start
a sudden stop
a long rest
qs.why: steady는 ‘일정한’이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why did the strangers along the road help Jiho?
o: Their cheers gave him energy when his legs ached.
They carried his bag to the finish line.
They told him the best route to take.
They gave him a warm coat to wear.
qs.why: “cheering strangers ... gave him new energy”라고 해요.

qs.q: Which word best describes Jiho's feeling at the end?
o: Satisfied
Embarrassed
Jealous
Bored
qs.why: 완주만으로 충분했다는 말에서 만족감을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: A Letter to the Principal
items.text: Dear Principal Han, We are writing on behalf of the Science Club to ask for permission to use the old greenhouse behind the gym. Left unused for years, it still has strong glass walls and a working water pipe. Our club wants to grow vegetables there, having seen how much food is thrown away in the cafeteria every day. Working together, we plan to give the first harvest to the cafeteria and the rest to a local food bank. We would clean and repair the greenhouse ourselves, asking only for the key and a few tools. We believe this project would teach students both science and responsibility. Thank you for considering our request. Sincerely, Yuna Seo, Club President

qs.q: Why is the club writing to the principal?
o: To ask permission to use a school space
To invite students to a science contest
To complain about the cafeteria menu
To report that the gym needs repairs
qs.why: 첫 문장에서 온실 사용 허가를 요청한다고 밝혀요.

qs.q: What condition is the greenhouse in?
o: Its walls and pipe still work.
Its roof has fallen in completely.
Its glass has been taken away.
Its door has been locked by the cooks.
qs.why: “still has strong glass walls and a working water pipe”라고 해요.

qs.q: What reason does the club give for growing vegetables?
o: They saw how much food is wasted at lunch.
They want to sell vegetables at a market.
They need a place to hold club meetings.
They were told to by the local food bank.
qs.why: “having seen how much food is thrown away in the cafeteria”가 이유예요.

qs.q: What will the club do with the first harvest?
o: Give it to the cafeteria
Sell it to other schools
Plant it again in the gym
Keep it for club members
qs.why: 첫 수확물은 급식실에 주겠다고 해요.

qs.q: How would you describe the tone of the letter?
o: Polite and well organized
Angry and demanding
Funny and careless
Sad and hopeless
qs.why: 공손한 표현과 구체적인 계획으로 정중하고 체계적인 어조예요.

items.title: Coral Reefs
items.text: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support about a quarter of all sea life. Built slowly by tiny animals called corals, a reef can take thousands of years to form. The corals live together with algae, which give them food and bright colors. When the water becomes too warm, stressed corals push out the algae and turn white, a process called bleaching. Bleached reefs are not dead, but they are weak. Given enough time and cooler water, they can recover. Unfortunately, warming seas, polluted rivers, and careless tourists, touching or breaking the coral, make recovery difficult in many places. Protecting reefs therefore requires action at local and global levels.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why coral reefs matter and what puts them at risk
How tourists can find the best reefs to visit
Why algae are more important than corals
How rivers carry sea animals to the open ocean
qs.why: 산호초의 중요성, 백화 현상, 위협 요인과 보호의 필요성을 다뤄요.

qs.q: What happens when the water gets too warm?
o: Corals push out algae and turn white.
Algae grow faster and cover the reef.
Corals move to colder parts of the ocean.
Tiny animals build a new reef quickly.
qs.why: “stressed corals push out the algae and turn white”라고 해요.

qs.q: “Bleached reefs are not dead, but they are weak” suggests that bleached reefs
o: may get better under good conditions
will soon be used for new buildings
cannot be seen from the surface
always recover within one season
qs.why: 죽은 것이 아니라 약해진 것이므로 조건이 좋아지면 회복할 수 있다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In “The corals live together with algae, which give them food and bright colors,” what does “them” refer to?
o: the corals
the tourists
the ocean floor
the algae
qs.why: which give them food에서 them은 먹이와 색을 받는 the corals를 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why does the writer use the word “Unfortunately”?
o: To introduce things that make recovery harder
To show that tourists protect the reefs
To say that reefs recover very fast
To describe how the corals get food
qs.why: 뒤에 회복을 어렵게 하는 요인들이 이어져요.

items.title: A Science Fair Mix-Up
items.text: On the morning of the science fair, Hojun carried his volcano model carefully into the gym, holding it with both hands. Placing it on the table, he realized that the baking soda was still sitting at home. Panicking, he called his sister, who arrived twenty minutes later on her bike, out of breath and carrying a small paper bag. Just before the judges reached his table, Hojun poured the vinegar. Nothing happened. The bag held flour, not baking soda. The judges, trying not to laugh, asked what had gone wrong. Hojun, smiling nervously, explained the whole story. To his surprise, they gave him a special prize for honesty.

qs.q: What did Hojun forget to bring to the fair?
o: The baking soda
The vinegar
The volcano model
The paper bag
qs.why: 집에 baking soda를 두고 왔다고 해요.

qs.q: Why did nothing happen when Hojun poured the vinegar?
o: His sister had brought the wrong powder.

items.title: Why Old Bridges Last
items.text: Walking across a stone bridge built five hundred years ago, you may wonder why it is still standing. The answer lies in its shape. Unlike a flat beam, an arch pushes the weight outward and downward, spreading the load along curved stones. Pressed tightly together, the stones lock in place, and the heavier the load, the tighter they hold. Builders of the past, working without modern math, learned these lessons by trial and error. Failed bridges taught them what worked. Today, engineers still copy the arch, though they build it with steel and concrete. Having proved its strength for centuries, the arch remains one of the safest shapes in construction.

qs.q: What is the main point of the passage?
o: The arch shape explains why old bridges stay strong.
Modern engineers have stopped using stone for bridges.
Flat beams are the safest shape for long bridges.
Past builders used math to make perfect bridges.

By reading books about modern math

By asking engineers of today for help

fall apart under pressure
